title: Reform cards and ranking grid
subject: History
unit: Summer 1: Victorian Britain and the Industrial Revolution (Revolution)
source: Seeded from history/y6 lesson 21 (Reform cards and ranking grid (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 21: Victorian reforms: the Factory Acts and public health. To understand how Victorian reforms improved life for workers, children and the poor

cards:
reform
a change to make things better

Act
a law passed by Parliament

Parliament
the group that makes the
country's laws

campaign
work to persuade people to
change something

compulsory
something you must do by law
blocks.task: use them to test yourself or a partner.

questions.q: Which law made school compulsory for 5 to 10 year olds?
questions.model: The 1870 Act built schools. The next step made going to school a must. That was in 1880.

questions.q: What did the Mines Act of 1842 do?
questions.a: Banned women and young children from working underground

questions.q: Who campaigned for the Factory Acts?
Make a reform ranking: place five reforms in order of significance and write a reason for your top and bottom choice in the portal response box.
questions.a: A ranking with two reasons using the three significance questions
questions.model: Teacher models the reason for the Education Act using the three questions.

questions.q: Why did reforms take so long to pass?
questions.a: Owners opposed them; Parliament was mostly rich men; it cost money

questions.q: Which Victorian reform still affects you today? How?
questions.a: For example: free schooling or clean water and sewers

questions.q: A law passed by Parliament is an:
Big question: how do laws change lives?
questions.a: They set rules everyone must follow, such as school for all and safer work
